her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give

The City Planner advised that Pascal Toupin- Selinger with Ironclad Developments has applied on behalf
of Andre Louis Cottyn to amend the zoning of 2844 Millstream Rd from the CS1 (Service Commercial) Zone
to the MUlA (Mixed Use Residential Commercial A) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to include the subject parcel in plans to construct an apartment building
on 720, 724 and 732 Meaford Avenue.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:


1.   That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
     unit, which may be reduced by 75% if rental tenure is secured for a term of no less than 10 years, prior
     to subdivision approval:


     a)     $2,562 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
     b)     $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of all
other charges on title, that agrees to the following:


           i.That the applicant provide a construction parking management plan, to the satisfaction of the
              Director of Engineering, prior to issuance of a building permit;
           ii.That the applicant provide a stormwater management plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of
              Engineering and in accordance with Bylaw No. 1000, prior to subdivision approval or building
              permit issuance, whichever is first;
          iii.That the applicant acknowledges and agrees to design the proposed development, in accordance
              to the updated parking regulations as determined by Council, to the discretion of the Director of
              Planning;
          iv.That the applicant agrees to implement the approved storm water management plan and to
              complete any required improvements and/or upgrades to on site and off site infrastructure
          necessary to facilitate proper drainage on the subject property at the applicant's expense;
       v.That the applicant will construct full frontage improvements, including, but not limited to, the
          installation of a sidewalk to the corner of Meaford and Millstream Road to align with the sidewalk
          infrastructure required along Meaford Road, in accordance with Bylaw No.1000 and to the
          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to subdivision approval or building permit
          issuance, whichever is first;
      vi.That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions or
          other required servicing requirements are to be fulfilled at the applicant's expense; and
      vii.That the applicant acknowledges the proximity to industrial business operators may be a nuisance
          to the future residents of the development;


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 516, (798 Goldstream Ave; 2747, 2753, 2761, 2769

The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1750 at 5:34 p.m.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his
or her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that after
everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be
heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Niall Paltiel of Island View Strategies has applied on behalf of Bishop of
Victoria Corporation (Our Lady of Rosary Catholic Church) to amend the zoning of 2747, 2753, 2761, 2769,
and 2779 Peatt Road; 2734, 2738, 2742, 2746, 2750, and 2756 Claude Road; and 798 Goldstream Avenue
from the P2 (Community Institutional), R1 (One-Family Residential), R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential)
Zone to a new C9 (Community Town Centre Pedestrian 9) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for a future mixed-used development on these properties
along with a new church and parish location.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1.
     a.    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
           residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:
                i.     $1,525 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                       $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund.

which case the applicant may request that Council amend Bylaw No. 1750 to include the contribution
amounts.

     b.    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
           square metre of commercial space, prior to issuance of a building permit:
                i.   $10.75 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.


     c.    That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the following:
                i.    A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately
                      managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director
                      of Engineering.
                      The registration of a lot consolidation plan that includes road dedication along Peatt
                      Road, Goldstream Avenue, and Claude Road to the satisfaction of the Manager of
                      Land Development and Director of Engineering;
                      The registration a blanket statutory right of way on the proposed church/assisted
                      living site for a pedestrian connection between Peatt Road and Claude Road; and
               iv.    The registration of a blanket statutory right of way on the southwest site for the
                      future installation of a pedestrian friendly plaza in the southwest corner, which would
                      include art work.
     d.   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority
          of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
                 i.   That a 2.0m wide pedestrian connection between Peatt Road and Claude Road be
                      constructed with red brick paves and lighting prior to issuance of a building permit,
                      to the satisfaction of the Parks Manager; and
                      That the southwest corner of the proposed commercial/residential site have a 300m2
                      pedestrian plaza with art work installed prior to issuance of a building permit, to the
                      satisfaction of the Director of Planning;
                      That a Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) be completed to the satisfaction of the
                      Director of Engineering for the full build-out of any block that commercial and/or
                      residential uses are proposed, prior to the issuance of building permit, and that the
                      recommendations of the TIA be implemented;
               iv.    That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provided to the
                      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of a building permit; and
                v.    That a storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building
                      permit and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of
                      Engineering;

source_identity.raw_motion_text:
That Council:

1.   Give 1st reading to the Bylaw No. 1749 to amend the zoning designation of the property located at 790
     McCallum from CH1 (Cluster Housing Residential) to a new MUE2 (Mixed-Use Employment 2) Zone with
     the addition of a three-storey height limit on townhouses and subject to the following terms and
     conditions:
            a) That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contribution
                 prior to issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval:

                     i.    The dedication of 16,200m2 of land in a block form and location to the satisfaction
                           of the Director of Planning; and
                    ii.    $1,000,000 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund for this site;
                           OR
                    iii.   An amenity building on this site to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning,
                           with a certified construction value of $1,000,000; and
                    iv.    $500,000 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund for this site;
                           OR
                    v.     Arts and Cultural structure(s) on this site to the satisfaction of the Director of
                           Planning with a certified construction value of $500,000.

              b)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the following:

                     i.    A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately
                           managed on-site for the proposed development, to the satisfaction of the
                           Director of Engineering.
                    ii     The registration a 10m wide statutory right of way along the western and
                           southern edges of the property for trail purposes; and
                   iii.    Road dedication at Treanor Avenue for the future construction of a roundabout
                           to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

              c)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered
                   in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

                                                                                                      January 8th, 2018
                                                                                                         Page 15 of 16


                   I.    That a four-way signalized intersection be installed on McCallum Road at the
                         main entry point to Costco (easterly) prior to issuance of a building permit or
                         subdivision approval;
                   ii.   That a roundabout be constructed along the frontage of this property on
                         Treanor Road prior to issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval, to
                         the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.
                  iii.   That a landscaped and irrigated trail be constructed along the southern and
                         western edges within the 10m wide statutory right of way to bylaw 1000
                         standards prior to issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval, and to
                         the satisfaction of the Manager of Parks;
                  iv.    That all road dedication including widening of McCallum Road and any new
                         internal municipal road is provided prior to issuance of a building permit or
                         subdivision approval to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering and
                         Approving Officer;
                  v.     That a Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) be completed prior to issuance of a
                         building permit or subdivision approval to the satisfaction of the Director of
                         Engineering for the proposed development, and that the recommendations of
                         the TIA be implemented;
                  vi.    That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provided prior to
                         issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval, to the satisfaction of the
                         Director of Engineering; and
                 vii.    That a storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building
                         permit or subdivision approval and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the
                         satisfaction of the Director of Engineering; AND

2.   Direct staff to release the existing 30m wide restrictive covenant in exchange for of a 10m wide statutory
     right of way for a buffer and trail.

       a)   BYLAW NO. 1748
            "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 514, (2844 Millstream Rd), 2017".


The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1748 at 5:32 p.m.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or
her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that after

                                                                                                      January 8th, 2018

everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be
heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Pascal Toupin- Selinger with Ironclad Developments has applied on behalf
of Andre Louis Cottyn to amend the zoning of 2844 Millstream Rd from the CS1 (Service Commercial) Zone
to the MUlA (Mixed Use Residential Commercial A) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to include the subject parcel in plans to construct an apartment building
on 720, 724 and 732 Meaford Avenue.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:


1.   That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
     unit, which may be reduced by 75% if rental tenure is secured for a term of no less than 10 years, prior
     to subdivision approval:


     a)     $2,562 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
     b)     $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of all
other charges on title, that agrees to the following:


           i.That the applicant provide a construction parking management plan, to the satisfaction of the
              Director of Engineering, prior to issuance of a building permit;
           ii.That the applicant provide a stormwater management plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of
              Engineering and in accordance with Bylaw No. 1000, prior to subdivision approval or building
              permit issuance, whichever is first;
          iii.That the applicant acknowledges and agrees to design the proposed development, in accordance
              to the updated parking regulations as determined by Council, to the discretion of the Director of
              Planning;
          iv.That the applicant agrees to implement the approved storm water management plan and to
              complete any required improvements and/or upgrades to on site and off site infrastructure
          necessary to facilitate proper drainage on the subject property at the applicant's expense;
       v.That the applicant will construct full frontage improvements, including, but not limited to, the
          installation of a sidewalk to the corner of Meaford and Millstream Road to align with the sidewalk
          infrastructure required along Meaford Road, in accordance with Bylaw No.1000 and to the
          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to subdivision approval or building permit
          issuance, whichever is first;
      vi.That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions or
          other required servicing requirements are to be fulfilled at the applicant's expense; and
      vii.That the applicant acknowledges the proximity to industrial business operators may be a nuisance
          to the future residents of the development;


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 516, (798 Goldstream Ave; 2747, 2753, 2761, 2769

The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1750 at 5:34 p.m.

contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that after

heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Niall Paltiel of Island View Strategies has applied on behalf of Bishop of
Victoria Corporation (Our Lady of Rosary Catholic Church) to amend the zoning of 2747, 2753, 2761, 2769,
and 2779 Peatt Road; 2734, 2738, 2742, 2746, 2750, and 2756 Claude Road; and 798 Goldstream Avenue
from the P2 (Community Institutional), R1 (One-Family Residential), R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential)

This is being proposed in order to allow for a future mixed-used development on these properties
along with a new church and parish location.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1.
     a.    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
           residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:
                i.     $1,525 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                       $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund.

Unless Council amends the Amenity Contribution policy prior to second reading of Bylaw No. 1750 in
which case the applicant may request that Council amend Bylaw No. 1750 to include the contribution
amounts.

     b.    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
           square metre of commercial space, prior to issuance of a building permit:
                i.   $10.75 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.


     c.    That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the following:
                i.    A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately
                      managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director
                      of Engineering.
                      The registration of a lot consolidation plan that includes road dedication along Peatt
                      Road, Goldstream Avenue, and Claude Road to the satisfaction of the Manager of
                      Land Development and Director of Engineering;
                      The registration a blanket statutory right of way on the proposed church/assisted
                      living site for a pedestrian connection between Peatt Road and Claude Road; and
               iv.    The registration of a blanket statutory right of way on the southwest site for the
                      future installation of a pedestrian friendly plaza in the southwest corner, which would
                      include art work.
     d.   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority
          of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
                 i.   That a 2.0m wide pedestrian connection between Peatt Road and Claude Road be
                      constructed with red brick paves and lighting prior to issuance of a building permit,
                      to the satisfaction of the Parks Manager; and
                      That the southwest corner of the proposed commercial/residential site have a 300m2
                      pedestrian plaza with art work installed prior to issuance of a building permit, to the
                      satisfaction of the Director of Planning;
                      That a Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) be completed to the satisfaction of the
                      Director of Engineering for the full build-out of any block that commercial and/or
                      residential uses are proposed, prior to the issuance of building permit, and that the
                      recommendations of the TIA be implemented;
               iv.    That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provided to the
                      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of a building permit; and
                v.    That a storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building
                      permit and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of
                      Engineering;


2.   Direct staff to enter into a shared parking agreement with owner(s) of the future church property
     that allows them exclusive privilege to the Danbrook parking lot on Sunday mornings and religions
     holidays in exchange for parking privileges of their private parking lot for the general public during
     daytime hours Monday to Friday, excluding religious holidays.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

concerns that the proposal is open ended. Would like to see more information on old and new housing
(site lines, traffic flow). The resident equated the proposal to signing a blank cheque. Also concerned
about the limit potential for solar panels on his roof, about removal of existing housing and where the
current folks will live and about the vastness of the proposal.

The Acting Mayor called a second time for presentations.

None presented.

Same resident raised concerns about existing renters and where they would live.

Jim Hartshorne (developer) — provided input, the Catholic Church subsidizes rentals.

Resident asked about public parking.

Matthew Baldwin (City Planner) — provided clarification to reciprocal agreement, as did Jim Hartshorne.

Another resident — raised concerns about notification and timing.

Niall Paltiel (developer) — Provided clarification and will give as much notice as possible. He also provided
clarification on behalf of the applicant.

There being no more presentations, the Acting Mayor officially declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No.
1750 closed at 5:57 p.m.
